text:
Marta (Support): Heads-up — we've got three support tickets that are basically the same ask: customers want streaming structured outputs from chat + first-class tool/function calling support in the streaming path. Tickets: https://support.redwood/c/4521, /4630, /4702
Alex (Product): Copy. Which customers? severity?
Marta (Support): FinCo (P1, blocking rollout), HealthApp (P2), RetailX (P2). FinCo is asking for partial structured frames so they can render intermediate UI while calls are executing.
Dina (Sales): FinCo has a renewal negotiation next month; they said this is a must-have to keep using hosted API. They'd pay for accelerated delivery but need clear acceptance criteria.
Alex (Product): Ok — high level ask: (1) stream tokens AND structured output frames (JSON objects) as they arrive, (2) allow function/tool call invocation mid-stream (i.e., signal tool call, run external, continue stream with tool result), (3) predictable ordering and simple fallbacks.
Leo (Eng): Technical concerns: current streaming path is token stream only. Function calling today is synchronous: model emits call, server collects, executes, then resumes. We don't have an IPC for partial structured frames + in-flight tool ops.
Marta (Support): Example flow from FinCo: they stream {event: "partial_answer", data: {blocks: [...]}} repeatedly; when model emits a tool_call frame we need an immediate "tool_request" frame with tool args, then a "tool_result" frame when done, then resume streaming continuation frames.
Alex (Product): Proposed acceptance criteria (for backlog):
- API: streaming endpoint supports discrete "frame" objects with type enum ["text","structured","tool_request","tool_result","done"].
- Backwards compat: clients that expect token streaming should continue to work (token frames still emitted).
- Tool calls: server signals tool_request with id and payload; platform allows out-of-band execution and accepts tool_result by id.
- Ordering: deterministic ordering guarantee for frames within a request; partial frames may be dropped by client but server should provide sequence IDs.
- SLA: no regression to median latency for simple non-tool streaming calls beyond 10%.
Alex (Product): Priority? I propose P0 for FinCo path (fast-track patch), P2 backlog for general GA.
Dina (Sales): We need estimate and a scoping doc to present to FinCo. If we can ship a finite-scope patch that supports a limited "tool proxy" (platform executes a single visible tool with <1s avg exec) within 4 weeks, they sign.
Leo (Eng): Rough engineering notes:
- Add framing protocol around existing chunk stream.
- Add per-request tool_request queue + callback hooks.
- Implement sequence IDs and a compact wire format to avoid token inflation.
- Edge cases: model requests nested tool calls, long-running tool_execs, user cancel.
- Risk: adds complexity to runtime scheduler + KV cache interactions.
Marta (Support): Quick workaround suggestion while we scope GA: transform service-side: parse token stream, detect special token markers, emit a pseudo-frame envelope to downstream clients via a compatibility flag. That would be a stopgap for FinCo if they can opt-in.
Alex (Product): Good idea. Two-track plan: 1) stopgap compatibility layer (opt-in) targeted at FinCo — low-risk, minimal infra changes; 2) spec work + API contract for proper framed streaming and tool lifecycle for GA.
Leo (Eng): For stopgap we can do a middleware that scans for a sentinel token sequence like "<<FRAME:{...}>>" in model output and converts to frames. Minimal runtime change. Est 5-7 dev days + tests.
Alex (Product): Next steps:
- @Leo (Eng) assign an engineer and create an RFC PR for the framed streaming API (include wire examples, error semantics, retry behavior).
- @Marta (Support) make a single consolidated ticket linking the three support tickets and include customer acceptance criteria.
- @Dina (Sales) confirm FinCo will accept opt-in compatibility layer and negotiate timeline/credits.
- I'll draft backlog epic and propose a canary rollout plan (start with opt-in, then beta customers, then GA).
Dina (Sales): Confirmed — I'll ping FinCo and ask for written sign-off if we commit to 4-week opt-in patch.
Marta (Support): Consolidated intake created: https://triage.redwood/INT-9876 — includes logs + sample transcripts.
Oncall Bot: Reminder: please schedule RFC review within 3 business days.
Leo (Eng): I'll slot discovery tasks on my team board. Est for full spec + implementation: 6-8 weeks depending on tooling tests.
Alex (Product): Thanks all. I'll create the epic and add acceptance criteria above. If anyone has strong objections to the two-track plan, call it out here now. :thumbsup:
Dina (Sales): :thumbsup:
Marta (Support): no objections
Leo (Eng): ok
Alex (Product): Filing now and assigning owners.
